rounds.text: Roadstar Infra Investment Trust offers compelling value through its asset backing, trading at a price-to-book ratio of just 0.72x against a book value of ₹ 86.0 per share [E1], which is further supported by a lower P/B multiple of 0.69x compared to the sector benchmark of 1.39x [E6]. Income-focused investors are well-rewarded by an attractive dividend yield of 8.55% [E3], while underlying cash generation is exceptionally robust with operating cash flow reaching ₹ 849 Cr and free cash flow hitting ₹ 797 Cr in March 2026 [E24, E25]. This cash generation efficiency is underscored by operating cash flow reaching 202% of operating profit [E26], paired with a comfortable short-term current ratio of 2.16x and a reduction in borrowings to ₹ 3,306 Cr [E28, E29]. Furthermore, operational momentum is surging, highlighted by a dramatic quarterly operating margin expansion to 68% in June 2026 and a strong relative-strength rating of 90 against the Nifty 500 [E20, E35]. conceded: [E8]

Roadstar Infra Investment Trust carries fundamental profitability risks that are masked by its asset-backed valuation [E1]. The business generates negative returns, posting an ROE of -5.6% [E12] and a 3-year median ROE of -2% [E17], with its ROCE lingering at a depressed 2.13% to 2.2% [E9, E11] against a sector benchmark of 6.61% [E9]. Operating performance is further compromised by a low interest coverage ratio [E44] and a structural margin compression that saw operating margins drop 12 percentage points from 62% to 50% over a three-year period [E19], alongside an inconsistent yearly margin trend [E21]. Conceded: [E25] Free cash flow reached Rs 797 Cr in Mar 2026.

The bear focuses on negative returns, but overlooks the massive cash generation that validates the asset backing, with free cash flow hitting ₹ 797 Cr and operating cash flow reaching ₹ 849 Cr in Mar 2026 [E25, E24]. Conceded: the ROE is negative at -5.6% and the 3-year median ROE is -2% [E12, E17], but this masks a powerful operational turnaround seen in the quarterly operating margin jumping to 68% in Jun 2026 from 17% a year prior (+51 percentage points) [E20]. While the bear cites depressed ROCE at 2.13% to 2.2% [E9, E11], borrowings actually decreased to ₹ 3,306 Cr from ₹ 3,669 Cr a year earlier, strengthening the balance sheet [E29]. Conceded: operating margins compressed over a three-year period [E19], yet trailing twelve-month profit growth accelerated by 20% alongside a 39% compounded sales growth over 3 years [E15, E13]. Furthermore, the low interest coverage concern [E44] is offset by a comfortable short-term liquidity current ratio of 2.16x and a discount valuation trading at 0.72x book value [E28, E1].

The bull relies on the massive operating cash flow of ₹ 849 Cr and free cash flow of ₹ 797 Cr for Mar 2026 [E24, E25], but cash conversion for that same period sits at an unmeaningful -3.11x due to a loss year, and the company is explicitly flagged for having a low interest coverage ratio [E23, E44]. Conceded: quarterly operating margin jumped to 68% in Jun 2026 from 17% a year prior [E20], yet the broader yearly operating-margin trend reads inconsistent, and operating margins have compressed by 12 percentage points over three years [E19, E21]. While borrowings decreased to ₹ 3,306 Cr [E29], the return metrics remain deeply distressed, featuring a negative ROE of -5.6%, a 3-year median ROE of -2%, and a weak ROCE of 2.13% to 2.2% that severely lags the sector median of 7.0% [E12, E17, E9, E11, E58].
